decisions.statement: A moment is kept beside the page of the service whose work landed.
A moment never reaches the commit.
A moment is written after the work of that round landed rather than before.
A round that ended part way through leaves the moment written before unmoved.
The moment being written is where a service leaves for code that moved.
That round has landed already, which is what makes the moment a safe point.
A service that has landed no round at all carries no moment.
How long a service may go between rounds is read off that service's page.
A service stating no window is judged by no moment.
A window that is zero seconds or shorter is no window.
A moment as old as the window is behind rather than kept.
A moment that is no instant is read as no moment rather than as a recent moment.
The key a moment is kept under is named here alone.
Nothing here settles which work counts as a round.
Nothing here says a service is broken or tells anyone so.

definition: the moment a service leaves published to say a round of its work landed
